faq: Can you work on a plugin another developer wrote?
Yes. We read the code first and tell you if anything is risky to change. We follow your naming and folder layout, so your own team can keep maintaining it after we finish.
Do you need access to my live store?
No. We work in your repository and on a staging copy. If you want us to test on your own staging site, add us as an administrator there. We never ask for your passwords.
Will my customers' existing settings survive the update?
Yes, that is a rule for us. We add upgrade routines where needed, test the update on a copy with real saved settings and tell you in the summary what was migrated.
Do you support PHP 8 and current WooCommerce?
Yes. New code targets current PHP and WooCommerce, including High-Performance Order Storage. If your plugin has older code that conflicts, we note it and can quote an upgrade.
desc:
WooCommerce plugin feature development means adding new features or fixing bugs inside a plugin that already exists. Ecom Swift LLC reads your code, agrees each change in writing, builds it in your repository and tests it before sending a pull request or updated zip.

## What is WooCommerce plugin feature development?

It is extending a working plugin without rewriting it. The change might be a new settings tab, an extra admin screen, a flow for a new kind of order, a set of hooks for other developers or a handful of bug fixes.

The work happens in your own code base, following your naming, structure and style. The goal is that your team can read the change, merge it and carry on as if one person had written it.

## Why is changing an existing plugin riskier than building a new one?

An existing plugin has users. Their settings, saved data and habits all depend on the current behavior. A change that renames an option or alters a database column can break stores that update. The user sees a blank screen or lost settings, and your support inbox fills.

There is also hidden knowledge in older code. Odd conditions often exist for a reason that nobody wrote down. Careful reading before writing is the best protection.

## How new features help your plugin grow

New features keep a plugin competitive. They answer support requests, open the plugin to new kinds of stores and give your Pro version more to offer. Bug fixes matter just as much, since a plugin with repeated errors loses trust faster than a plugin that lacks one feature.

Developer-friendly hooks and filters add another kind of value. When other developers can extend your plugin safely, they build on top of it instead of replacing it.

## What good plugin feature work includes

- A written list of changes, each described and approved before coding.
- Code that follows your existing style and the WordPress coding standards.
- Existing settings migrated safely, with defaults for new options.
- An update routine that works on stores already using the plugin.
- New admin screens or tabs that match the current interface.
- Hooks and filters that let other developers extend the new feature.
- Database tables with an upgrade routine, where storage is needed.
- Testing on a staging copy with current WooCommerce and common themes.
- Automated tests for new code, in higher packages.
- A changelog entry and a version bump.

## What we do

You share the repository or a zip and a list of the changes you want. We read the relevant code, then reply with a written plan that says what will change, which files are touched and which risks exist. Once you approve it, we build.

We test on a staging copy, including an update from an older version with real-looking data, since that is where problems usually appear. You receive a pull request or an updated zip and a short summary of the changes. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in the number of features and fixes, the number of new screens, and whether database changes, tests and release notes are included.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Give us access to the repository, or a recent copy of the code.
- List the changes in priority order.
- Tell us about the older versions that must keep working.
- Keep existing option names stable.
- Review the pull request and merge it in small steps.

**Avoid:**
- Sending a vague wish list with no priorities.
- Changing the same files in parallel while we work.
- Removing old settings without a migration.
- Testing only with a fresh install.
- Releasing straight to every user without a staged rollout.

## Who this service is for

This service suits a plugin owner whose original developer is no longer available. It suits a team with a backlog of feature requests and not enough development time. It also suits an agency that maintains a client plugin and needs a specialist for one larger change.

## What we need from you

Send repository access or a zip, the list of changes, and any notes on the plugin's history. Tell us which WooCommerce and PHP versions you support. We never ask for passwords. Access to the code is given through a collaborator account, and you do not need to give us your live store.
